text:
maria: noticed an uptick in duplicate resume traces after the eu canary bump. telemetry shows billing counter increments with two active sockets for the same resume token :thinking_face:
jamal: which canary and what was changed?
maria: proxy idle_close reduced 45->30s to reclaim sockets faster. canary id 1861009000. traces show proxy sending FIN then client reopens with same resume token and runtime creates a new session
maria: log snippet:```
[proxy] 2026-03-23T12:05:31Z conn=zz FIN_SENT idle_close=30s route=sticky-eu
[runtime] 2026-03-23T12:05:31Z session=xyz resume=tok-77 kv_cache=hit
[client] 2026-03-23T12:05:32Z reconnect resume=tok-77 -> new session created billable=true
```
sonya: we intentionally shortened idle_close for the canary to free up ports. didn't think resume flow would create a billing race. :grimacing:
mikhael: some SDKs treat a server FIN as terminal and drop client-side state; others try to resume. combined with sticky routing TTL, we can temporarily have two live sessions referencing same resume token
naima: CS flagged three customers with doubled streaming usage this morning. they're pretty unhappy.
jamal: short-term mitigations: a) reject duplicate resume within Xs and force reconnect, b) make runtime resume idempotent when client fingerprint matches (non-billable attach), c) add console-level dedupe to avoid alert storms and hide transient churn
sonya: (ops) b) seems safest long term but needs billing reconciliation. a) is risky UX-wise. c) is quickest for alert noise
maria: telemetry recommends combination: console dedupe for 30s, runtime accept-reattach for matching fingerprint, proxy feature-flag to avoid half-close if resume token present
mikhael: agree. runtime change must guarantee O(1) token lookup and add an audit event when reattach happens so billing can replay if needed
jamal: sketch for runtime:```python
def handle_resume(req):
    tok = req.headers.get('x-resume-token')
    if token_db.exists(tok) and fingerprint_ok(req):
        metrics.increment('runtime.resume.attach')
        return attach_session(tok, req, billable=False)
    return create_session(req)
```
sonya: proxy FF: "suppress-halfclose-if-resume" default off, enable in canary. careful with proxy pools and connection recycling
naima: I'll coordinate comms to affected accounts and include timeframe for canary hotfix
maria: console change: add alert annotation "possible resume churn during rollout" + add rule param dedupe_window=30s for streaming-heartbeat. mikhael can you add UX note in the console incident drawer?
mikhael: yep will add an orange banner for SREs and set dedupe_window=30s for tenant group filter
deploy-bot: deploy requested: canary/runtime/reattach-nonbillable -> queued on eng-runtime-canary
jamal: I'll open PR and add an e2e that simulates server FIN + client resume + sticky routing to catch regressions
sonya: rolling FF to 10% for proxy to start, runtime canary to eng-runtime-canary. monitor billing counters and resume.attach metric
maria: timeline: canary today 2h, then 50% if metrics look good, full rollout EOD. keep console alerts muted for impacted tenants during canary window to avoid noise
naima: pinging CS slack channel to let them know we have a fix path and timeline
jamal: also adding a short-lived billing dedupe job that watches for duplicate session_ids within 60s window and marks duplicates non-billable retroactively if attach event present
mikhael: logging: add resume.attach audit log with tenant_id, resume_token, fingerprint, session_before, session_after. important for postmortem and for billing reconciliation
maria: good. let's reconvene after first canary batch. thanks team :heart:
